case_name: Prathiv Singh vs State (Home Department)Ors on 6 December, 2012

legal_principles.principle: The welfare of the child is the paramount consideration in matters of custody.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that the welfare of the child is the paramount consideration in matters of custody. The court's primary concern is to ensure that the child's interests are protected and that the child is placed in a situation where he or she can grow and develop in a healthy and happy environment.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 — Section 7

legal_principles.principle: The court will not interfere with a parent's decision regarding the upbringing and education of their child unless it is shown that such interference is necessary to protect the child from harm.
legal_principles.held: This Court has consistently held that the court will not interfere with a parent's decision regarding the upbringing and education of their child unless it is shown that such interference is necessary to protect the child from harm. The court's role is limited to ensuring that the child's interests are protected, but it will not intervene in matters which do not affect the child's welfare.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 — Section 7
cited_cases: Rajesh Kumar v. Sangeeta Kumari, (2013) 10 SCC 511
